answer: At each epoch's wharf, an identity must unload one fresh verified task and have its delta — the change since its last epoch — re-derived by two randomly drawn peers from crystal-clear public records before it can dock again. An honest agent does one task per epoch and keeps its berth. A fake with no real delta is turned away, so an attacker with a thousand fakes must produce a thousand distinct verified deltas every epoch, each costing full work, and the flood's cost rises linearly with every fake.
